title: Good and bad bishops
summary: A bishop is bad when your own pawns stand on its colour. Free it, trade it, or keep your pawns on the other colour.
body:
### Your pawns decide your bishop

A bishop stays on one colour of squares. Your pawns decide if it is good or bad.

- **Bad bishop.** Many of your pawns stand on the same colour as the bishop. The pawns block its diagonals. The bishop does little.
- **Good bishop.** Your pawns stand on the other colour. The bishop has open diagonals and can attack.

Look at the Slav and Caro-Kann. Black has pawns on c6, d5 and e6. They all stand on light squares. So Black's light-squared bishop is bad if it stays behind them. Now look at the London. White has pawns on c3, d4 and e3. They stand on dark squares. So White's light-squared bishop is good.

How to fix a bad bishop:

- Bring it outside the pawn chain before you play ...e6. The Caro-Kann bishop goes to f5 (lesson 11).
- Change the pawns. In the Semi-Slav, ...dxc4 gives up the d5 pawn. Then ...b5 and ...Bb7 bring the bishop to the long diagonal, and ...c5 opens it.
- Trade it for a piece that matters.

How to keep a good bishop good:

- Put your pawns on the colour opposite to your bishop.
- Do not trade it for a knight without a reason (lesson 7).
- Aim it at weak enemy pawns on its colour.

You can find the colour of a square quickly. A1 is dark. Squares next to each other have different colours.

Rule of thumb: keep your pawns on the colour opposite to your bishop, and free a bad bishop before it gets locked in.

exercises.prompt: Black to move. Bring your light-squared bishop outside the pawn chain, and attack the knight on e4.
exercises.explanation: Bf5 puts the bishop outside the pawn chain before ...e6 locks it in. It also attacks the knight on e4.

exercises.prompt: Black to move. Your light-squared bishop is shut in by your pawns on c6, d5 and e6. Start to free it with a pawn capture.
exercises.explanation: dxc4 gives up the pawn on d5. If White takes back with Bxc4, ...b5 attacks the bishop and prepares ...Bb7. The bishop gets out of its prison.

exercises.prompt: Black to move. Your light-squared bishop can leave c8 now. Put it on the long diagonal.
exercises.explanation: Bb7 puts the bishop on the long diagonal a8-h1. The c6 pawn still blocks it, so Black plans ...c5 to open the diagonal.
